A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and segmentation evaluations, resolution and target-granularity experiments, discard tests, and spatial and noise analyses, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an upstream-versus-downstream uncertainty-distribution analysis in Appendix M and Figure 15.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same frozen representations, MLP uncertainty module, ranking objective, and token-wise spatial uncertainty procedure. The added explanation of the scalar uncertainty output does not change the method.

E1.justification: Dataset, task, geographic, modality, and noisy-data coverage remain unchanged. The new distribution analysis reuses existing upstream and downstream datasets; multispectral and SAR experiments were already present in v1 Appendix E.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ImageNet, BigEarthNet, BigEarthNet-5, and Flair pretraining configurations, with the same random reference where applicable. The added density analysis introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds a diagnostic procedure comparing uncertainty distributions from a BigEarthNet-pretrained ViT-Large across upstream and downstream datasets. Existing training settings, LA-CPA evaluations, resolution experiments, and 200-step discard tests remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the distribution-shift diagnostic in Appendix M/Figure 15 to investigate whether uncertainty reflects epistemic signals. Existing granularity, resolution, noise, and localized-uncertainty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The new density plot describes distributions of predicted uncertainty across samples, rather than statistical uncertainty around experimental results.

E6.justification: Figure 15 newly reports broader, higher upstream BigEarthNet uncertainties and low MARIDA uncertainties despite domain shift. Matched benchmark tables and existing plotted findings remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 2–5 becoming v2 Tables 4–7.

T1.justification: The loss equations, LA@1 definitions, Hellinger-based metrics, CPA explanation, and monotonicity-fraction formula are retained. Corrected metric terminology and explicit mention of averaging restate mathematics already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution statements retain the same evaluation framework, EO generalization findings, GSD sensitivity, downstream utility, and spatial uncertainty extension. Emphasis on aleatoric uncertainty does not redefine these contributions; v1 already described the method as targeting aleatoric uncertainty.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 reframes noise sensitivity as evidence of aleatoric uncertainty, and Appendix M interprets the added distributions as showing a lack of epistemic signals. The conclusion also explicitly identifies image-level representation training as a limitation for spatial uncertainty and proposes dense-task training.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix J/Table 6 reappears as v2 Appendix G/Table 3 with unchanged architecture, hyperparameters, optimizer, and 1000-epoch schedule. Code and pretrained-weight disclosures remain the same. The new experiment overview consolidates previously documented settings.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects its aleatoric-versus-epistemic diagnostic to Kirchhof et al. [31], describing Appendix M as a replication of their analysis. This adds a limited relationship to prior findings; the same 53 references and broader EO research positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, retitles Section 4.5, adds explanatory appendix sections, and moves training details earlier in the supplement. Affiliations and acknowledgments are updated, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially through illustrations of all four semantic factors (Figures 10–13), an experiment overview table, and the new density plot. Existing plots are rendered more sharply, Figure 3 panels are reordered, Figure 5 titles specify image sizes, and several figures and tables are relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: The added distribution diagnostic, clearer spatial-uncertainty limitation, semantic-factor illustrations, and experiment overview modestly improve interpretation and readability. The core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. The assertion that epistemic uncertainty is absent exceeds what the single-model distribution comparison establishes, limiting the scientific gain.
